statewide.description: The Governor is Vermont's chief executive, responsible for managing state government, signing or vetoing legislation, appointing judges and cabinet members, and representing Vermont in national affairs.

candidates.name: June Goodband
candidates.bio: Ran for Governor in 2024 as the Green Mountain Peace and Justice Party candidate.

candidates.name: Amanda Janoo
candidates.bio: An Oxford-trained economist and Strafford native, running for office for the first time.
notablePositions: Proposes publicly funded universal primary care, with the state paying providers directly
Would fund it with income-tax surcharges on high earners — 2% on income over $250,000 and 8% over $500,000

candidates.name: Brian Judd
candidates.bio: Barre City resident. Ran for Barre City Council in 2021 and was a Republican candidate for the Vermont House (Washington-3) in 2022.

candidates.name: Dean Roy
candidates.bio: Stowe student, Freedom and Unity Party nominee.
notablePositions: Helped form the Freedom and Unity Party in 2026

candidates.name: Phil Scott
candidates.bio: Phil Scott has served as Vermont's Governor since January 2017, winning five consecutive two-year terms. A former contractor and racing driver, Scott is a Republican who has supported abortion rights and signed gun safety legislation while vetoing several Democratic tax and spending proposals.
notablePositions: Supports abortion rights
Has signed gun safety legislation
Has vetoed several Democratic tax and spending proposals
Focus on housing affordability and economic development

statewide.description: The Lieutenant Governor presides over the Vermont Senate (but only votes to break ties), serves on several state boards, and becomes Governor if the Governor is unable to serve.

candidates.name: Molly Gray
candidates.bio: Former Vermont Lieutenant Governor (2021–2023).

candidates.name: John S. Rodgers
candidates.bio: John Rodgers was elected Lieutenant Governor in 2024 running as a Republican, after years as a Democratic state senator. He previously served in the Vermont House and Senate representing the Northeast Kingdom and has long advocated for Second Amendment rights.
notablePositions: Supports Second Amendment rights
Switched from Democrat to Republican before the 2024 race
Focus on rural Vermont issues and the Northeast Kingdom
Advocates for workforce development and economic opportunity

statewide.description: The Attorney General is Vermont's chief law enforcement officer, representing the state in legal matters, enforcing consumer protection laws, and prosecuting public corruption.

candidates.name: Charity R. Clark
candidates.bio: Charity Clark was elected Vermont Attorney General in 2022, becoming the first woman to hold the office. She previously served as Chief Assistant Attorney General. She has been active in multi-state coalitions on opioids, environmental protection, and consumer fraud.
notablePositions: First woman to serve as Vermont Attorney General
Active in multi-state opioid and environmental enforcement actions
Focus on consumer protection and corporate accountability

candidates.name: Edwin Howell Kemon
candidates.bio: Vergennes resident who works as a digital model-based systems engineer. Named the Republican nominee by the state party committee in August 2026 after H. Brooke Paige, who won the primary, withdrew from this race.
notablePositions: Says he would focus the office on public safety, government accountability, consumer protection, and environmental enforcement
Says he would prioritize crimes against children, including trafficking, and end "catch and release of repeat offenders"
Says he would move the office away from "high-volume litigation against the federal administration"

statewide.notes: H. Brooke Paige won the Republican primary for Attorney General and later withdrew; Edwin Howell Kemon is the Republican nominee on the November ballot.

statewide.description: The Secretary of State oversees Vermont's elections, maintains official state records, regulates professional licenses, and registers businesses and nonprofits.

candidates.name: Sarah Copeland Hanzas
candidates.bio: Sarah Copeland Hanzas was first elected Secretary of State in 2022. She previously served in the Vermont House of Representatives for over a decade. She succeeded Jim Condos, who served as Secretary of State from 2011–2022.
notablePositions: Expanded access to absentee voting
Modernized business registration systems
Advocates for election security and voter access

candidates.name: H. Brooke Paige
candidates.bio: Washington resident and retired sales and marketing CEO; serves as a justice of the peace and on his town's Board of Civil Authority. Won four Republican statewide primaries in August 2026 and withdrew from all but Secretary of State.
notablePositions: Says the Secretary of State's office has taken control of elections away from local officials, citing universal vote-by-mail
Favors streamlining the office's Business Services and Office of Professional Regulation

candidates.name: Rachel Shaw
candidates.bio: Bennington resident since 2023 who works in hospitality and sales and marketing. Served in the Massachusetts Army National Guard and studied emergency management at Massachusetts Maritime Academy. Says she is focused on housing, health care, education, and affordability.

statewide.notes: H. Brooke Paige won four Republican primaries in August (Treasurer, Secretary of State, Auditor, and Attorney General) and later withdrew from three of them. Secretary of State is the one he's still on the ballot for.

statewide.description: The State Treasurer manages Vermont's finances, investments, and public debt, and administers retirement funds for state employees and teachers.

candidates.name: Zachary Hampl
candidates.bio: Rutland Town resident, an author and financial account manager who has also sold insurance. Won the Progressive primary for treasurer unopposed.
notablePositions: Supports a state-owned bank modeled on North Dakota's, or a "collaborative banking system"
Names responsible funding of state employee pensions as a key challenge

candidates.name: Lynn LaFleur
candidates.bio: Stowe accountant, tax preparer, and controller. Treasurer of the Vermont Republican Party, former chair of the Lamoille County Republican Committee, and a Stowe justice of the peace. Named the Republican nominee by the state party committee in August 2026.
notablePositions: Says she would address state pension underfunding as a way to lower school property taxes
Says the office should return unclaimed property more proactively
Pledges plain-language public financial reporting

candidates.name: Mike Pieciak
candidates.bio: Mike Pieciak was first elected State Treasurer in 2022. He previously served as Commissioner of the Vermont Department of Financial Regulation and oversaw Vermont's pandemic stimulus distribution before becoming Treasurer.
notablePositions: Focus on fiscal responsibility and pension fund management
Advocates for Vermont housing investment programs

statewide.notes: H. Brooke Paige won the Republican primary for Treasurer and later withdrew; Lynn LaFleur is the Republican nominee on the November ballot.

statewide.description: The Auditor of Accounts independently audits Vermont state agencies, ensuring taxpayer money is spent efficiently, legally, and as intended. The Auditor reports to the legislature and the public — not the Governor.

candidates.name: Tim Ashe
candidates.bio: Tim Ashe has served as Chief Deputy Auditor of Accounts since 2021. He was previously Vermont Senate President Pro Tem from 2013–2021 and ran for Lieutenant Governor in 2020.
notablePositions: Chief Deputy Auditor of Accounts since 2021
Former Vermont Senate President Pro Tem (2013–2021)
Ran for Lt. Governor in 2020

candidates.name: Ivar Kronick
candidates.bio: Poultney resident who manages finances and audits for a company with about $3 million in operations. Named the Republican nominee by the state party committee in August 2026.
notablePositions: Says Health and Human Services and Medicaid need more audit scrutiny
Proposes one searchable public list of all audits, findings, recommendations, and follow-ups
Says he would publicly post fraud, waste, and abuse referrals to the Attorney General

statewide.notes: H. Brooke Paige won the Republican primary for Auditor and later withdrew; Ivar Kronick is the Republican nominee on the November ballot.

federal.description: Vermont has a single at-large congressional seat in the U.S. House of Representatives. One representative covers the entire state, serving on congressional committees, voting on federal legislation, and directing federal funding to Vermont.

candidates.name: Phoenix K. Altair
candidates.bio: Grassroots organizer running for Congress as an independent; first run for this seat.
notablePositions: Says term limits "should apply to all positions"
Calls for ending privatized prisons
Calls for better rural infrastructure, including cell towers and internet service

candidates.name: Becca Balint
candidates.bio: Becca Balint was elected Vermont's at-large U.S. Representative in 2022, becoming the first woman and first openly gay person elected to Congress from Vermont. She previously served in the Vermont Senate and as Senate President Pro Tem. She serves on the House Judiciary Committee and House Education and Workforce Committee.
notablePositions: First woman and first openly LGBTQ+ person elected to Congress from Vermont
Former Vermont Senate President Pro Tem
Serves on House Judiciary Committee
Focus on housing, climate, and workers' rights

candidates.name: Gerald Malloy
candidates.bio: Army veteran; previously the 2022 Republican nominee for U.S. Senate against Peter Welch.

candidates.name: Adam Ortiz
candidates.bio: U.S. Army veteran who served in the Army National Guard from 2006 to 2012. Also ran for this seat as an independent in 2022 and 2024.
notablePositions: Suggests replacing Social Security with "a mandatory savings account where you get out what you put in"
Says much of the national debt could be renegotiated

candidates.name: Suzanne "Suz" Seymour
candidates.bio: Massage therapist, small-business owner, and comedian running for Congress as an independent. Says her campaign takes no PAC money.
notablePositions: Proposes spending caps and fraud audits, and cutting or freezing congressional pay until Congress passes a balanced budget
Says Congress should use its war powers and that "peace through diplomacy is the best way"
Calls for audits of how Social Security money has been managed

candidates.name: Ryan P. Walton
candidates.bio: Software developer who says he has also restored properties, created housing, and run service businesses. Says he is running to give Vermont an independent voice that owes "neither party a vote."
notablePositions: Accepts contributions only from Vermont residents, capped at $250, with no PAC, party, or corporate money
Lists Vermont's housing shortage among his focus areas

stateSenate.description: The Vermont State Senate has 30 members who serve 2-year terms. The Chittenden Southeast district elects 3 senators, who pass state legislation, approve the state budget, and confirm the Governor's key appointments.
stateSenate.voteForNote: This district elects three senators, so you can vote for up to three candidates — from any party, in any combination.

candidates.name: Thomas Chittenden
candidates.bio: Thomas Chittenden grew up in South Burlington and previously served on the South Burlington City Council. He was elected to the Vermont Senate representing Chittenden Southeast.
notablePositions: Former South Burlington City Councilor
Grew up in South Burlington

candidates.name: Kesha Ram Hinsdale
candidates.bio: Kesha Ram Hinsdale has been Senate Majority Leader since January 2025. She served in the Vermont House from 2009 to 2016 and has been in the Senate since 2021. She is the first woman of color to serve in the Vermont Senate.
notablePositions: Senate Majority Leader since January 2025
First woman of color to serve in the Vermont Senate
Focus on climate, housing, and racial equity

candidates.name: Virginia "Ginny" Lyons
candidates.bio: Virginia Lyons is a Vermont State Senator representing the Chittenden Southeast district. She has served in the Senate for multiple terms.
notablePositions: Chittenden Southeast representative

candidates.name: Bruce Roy
candidates.bio: Retired IBM engineer and Air Force veteran.

candidates.name: Javen Sears
candidates.bio: UVM student and South Burlington High School class of 2020 graduate.
notablePositions: Recent SBHS graduate (2020)
UVM student

candidates.name: Rohan St Marthe
candidates.bio: Jericho resident. Was the Republican candidate for this Senate district in 2022 and 2024.

stateSenate.notes: Rohan St Marthe won a Republican nomination as a write-in candidate in the August primary.

notablePositions: First-term representative (elected 2024)
South Burlington representative

notablePositions: South Burlington representative

notablePositions: South Burlington representative

stateHouse.districtNote: Covers part of South Burlington. Not sure which district you're in? Look it up at mvp.vermont.gov.

candidates.name: Brian Minier
candidates.bio: Brian Minier represents a South Burlington district in the Vermont House of Representatives.
notablePositions: South Burlington representative

stateHouse.districtNote: Covers part of South Burlington. Not sure which district you're in? Look it up at mvp.vermont.gov.

candidates.name: Martin J. LaLonde
candidates.bio: Martin LaLonde is a South Burlington attorney who has served in the Vermont House for several terms.
notablePositions: Attorney by profession
Multi-term South Burlington representative

stateHouse.districtNote: Covers part of South Burlington. Not sure which district you're in? Look it up at mvp.vermont.gov.

candidates.name: Sarah George
candidates.bio: Has served as Chittenden County State's Attorney since 2017 and is seeking a third full term.
notablePositions: Pairs accountability with treatment courts and recovery services
Emphasizes reentry support for people leaving the justice system

candidates.name: Jace Laquerre
candidates.bio: Milton software engineer who says he is not an attorney. Was one of Vermont's delegates to the 2016 Republican National Convention.
notablePositions: Says that if elected he would resign immediately so the governor could appoint a replacement

county.notes: Bram Kranichfeld won the Republican nomination as a write-in candidate in August and later withdrew; Jace Laquerre is the Republican nominee on the November ballot.

Vermont Secretary of State — 2026 General Election qualified candidates (updated Sept 23, 2026)

candidates.name: Daniel Gamelin
candidates.bio: Has served as Chittenden County Sheriff since being elected in 2022, with more than 40 years in the sheriff's department.
notablePositions: Elected sheriff in 2022
More than 40 years in the sheriff's department

county.notes: Daniel Gamelin won the Democratic primary and also won the Republican nomination as a write-in candidate.

noteSources.title: Vermont Secretary of State — 2026 August Primary winner listing (official)

candidates.name: Paul McManus
candidates.bio: Williston resident who spent 32 years with the Chittenden County Sheriff's Office. Has also served as a regional area commander for the Federal Protective Service and as director of security for the Vermont Department of Buildings and General Services.
notablePositions: Says the high bailiff should be present in the community and know how the sheriff's office operates

candidates.name: Amy Payne
candidates.bio: Burlington resident and former publishing executive and educator. In her second term as Burlington's Ward 4 inspector of elections and has co-led restorative justice work.
notablePositions: Says the high bailiff should be a civilian rather than a law-enforcement official
Says she would act as a bridge between the sheriff's office and the community, and work with whichever sheriff is elected

county.notes: Amy Payne won the Democratic primary. Paul McManus won the Republican nomination as a write-in candidate.

candidates.name: Connie Cain Ramsey
candidates.bio: Incumbent assistant judge, first elected in November 2010. A member of the National Association of County Judges and the Vermont Association of Assistant Judges, and writes the "Courthouse Chronicles" historical articles.

county.notes: Both won the Democratic primary and also won Republican nominations as write-in candidates.

candidates.name: Gregory J. Glennon
candidates.bio: Incumbent probate judge, appointed by Gov. Peter Shumlin in 2016 after serving as general counsel to the Vermont Agency of Education. Previously practiced law in South Burlington and was an assistant district attorney in Suffolk County, Mass.
